title: siRNA vs miRNA and Epigenetic Silencing
summary: Learn how siRNA and miRNA use the same Dicer and RISC machinery but reach different fates through perfect versus seed pairing, and how DNA methylation and histone marks change gene activity without changing the DNA sequence.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 68 Hits 5 and 8 and Exam Trap 2. It also covers the siRNA vs miRNA row of the Do Not Confuse table (Table 2), but only that row, so Table 2 and the Do Not Confuse section are not claimed as taught here. Checked against Lam 2015, O’Brien 2018 and Kondo 2009 (Europe PMC full text) and Moore 2013 (read via a page-fetch tool; first part of the page only). Context added: the reviewer says miRNA causes “translational blockade” rather than degradation; Lam 2015 and O’Brien 2018 say miRNA silencing works through translational repression and mRNA deadenylation, decapping and decay (no AGO2 slicing), so the lesson teaches “muffle, then often clear” (register flag rv-mirna-repression-plus-decay). The reviewer’s sizes (“both 22–26 nt, cut by Dicer into 21–24 nt fragments”) do not match the sources (siRNA 21–23 nt, Lam 2015; miRNA duplex 18–25 nt, Lam 2015; mature miRNA average 22 nt, O’Brien 2018); the lesson uses the source values (register flag rv-sirna-mirna-size-range). The reviewer’s “bulging” wording is not taught. Not taught: therapeutics, RNAi delivery, specific histone residues.

objectives: Describe how Dicer and RISC/Argonaute process siRNA and miRNA.
Predict the fate of a target mRNA from perfect versus seed (imperfect) pairing.
Define epigenetics and explain how promoter CpG methylation and histone marks affect transcription.

scenes.title: Same gene, three ways to quiet it
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: a research lab studies gene X in cultured cells. (1) RNA A, fully complementary to the gene X mRNA, is added: the mRNA level collapses. (2) RNA B, matching gene X only through a short seed region in the 3′ UTR, is added: protein falls and the mRNA level also falls. (3) In a tumour sample, gene X is silent although its DNA sequence is normal. Question token: “Slice, muffle, or switch off?”

cues.text: Invented scenario. A lab adds a small RNA that matches gene X perfectly, and the gene X messenger RNA collapses.
A second small RNA matches only through a short seed region. Protein falls, and the messenger RNA level falls too.
In a tumour, gene X is silent although its DNA sequence is normal. Slice, muffle, or switch off?

scenes.title: Two small RNAs, one machine
scenes.altText: Schematic pathway. siRNA: long double-stranded RNA is cut by Dicer into a 21–23-nt siRNA duplex with 2-nt 3′ overhangs; it loads into RISC, Argonaute 2 (AGO2) cleaves and removes the passenger strand, and the guide strand stays. miRNA: transcribed by RNA polymerase II as a pri-miRNA, cut by Drosha/DGCR8 to a hairpin pre-miRNA, exported by Exportin 5, cut by Dicer to a duplex (average mature length about 22 nt); one strand loads into Argonaute to form miRISC. Both silence genes after transcription by targeting mRNA.

cues.text: Both small RNAs silence genes after transcription, by guiding a protein complex to messenger RNA.

siRNA starts as long double-stranded RNA. Dicer cuts it into a duplex of about twenty-one to twenty-three nucleotides, which loads into RISC. Argonaute 2 removes the passenger strand and keeps the guide strand.

miRNA comes from the cell’s own genes. Drosha trims the primary transcript to a hairpin, Exportin 5 moves it to the cytoplasm, and Dicer cuts it to a duplex. Mature miRNAs average about twenty-two nucleotides.
One strand of the miRNA loads into an Argonaute protein to form miRISC. Same core machinery, so what decides the outcome?

props.label: Same machine: what decides the fate?

scenes.title: Fit decides fate
scenes.altText: Two duplex drawings (schematic). Left: siRNA guide strand fully complementary to its target, usually in the coding region; AGO2 cleaves the mRNA between positions 10 and 11 relative to the guide 5′ end; fragments are degraded by exonucleases; one specific target. Right: miRNA pairs mainly through its 5′ seed region with the 3′ UTR; central mismatches prevent AGO2 slicing; GW182 recruits deadenylases (PAN2–PAN3, CCR4–NOT), then decapping and 5′→3′ decay, plus translational repression; one miRNA can regulate many mRNAs. Small note: rarely, a highly complementary miRNA site is cleaved.

cues.text: Fit decides fate. siRNA is fully complementary to one target. That perfect pairing activates Argonaute 2, which slices the messenger RNA, and the pieces are degraded.
Most miRNA sites pair mainly through the seed region near the miRNA’s five-prime end, usually in the three-prime untranslated region. Central mismatches block slicing.
Instead, miRISC represses translation and recruits deadenylases, so the poly-A tail is removed, the cap is taken off, and the messenger RNA decays. Muffled, then often cleared.
Because perfect pairing is not needed, one miRNA regulates many targets; an siRNA is designed for one. Rarely, a highly complementary miRNA site is sliced like an siRNA target.

scenes.title: Epigenetics: switching genes off
scenes.altText: Schematic promoter. Epigenetics: heritable changes in gene activity without a change in DNA sequence. DNA methyltransferases add a methyl group to carbon 5 of cytosine (5-methylcytosine) at CpG sites. Promoter CpG islands are normally unmethylated; their methylation stably silences the gene. Methyl-CpG-binding proteins such as MeCP2 recruit histone deacetylases, and tightly packed chromatin is less permissive for transcription. Histone tails carry acetylation (generally open, active chromatin) and methylation (activating or repressive depending on the residue). Hook answer card: RNA A = siRNA-type slicing; RNA B = miRNA-type muffling; tumour = epigenetic silencing, such as promoter hypermethylation of a tumour-suppressor gene.

cues.text: Epigenetics means heritable changes in gene activity without any change in the DNA sequence. The classic mark is DNA methylation: a methyl group added to carbon five of cytosine at CpG sites, making five-methylcytosine.

Promoter CpG islands are normally unmethylated. When they become methylated, the gene is stably silenced. Methyl-binding proteins recruit histone deacetylases, and tightly packed chromatin resists transcription.
Histone tails carry marks too. Acetylation generally opens chromatin and goes with active genes; histone methylation can activate or repress, depending on which residue is marked.
Back to the hook. RNA A sliced its target, RNA B muffled it, and the tumour gene was switched off epigenetically: cancers use promoter hypermethylation to silence tumour-suppressor genes.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “miRNA slices its target like siRNA” (✓ imperfect seed pairing blocks AGO2 slicing; miRNA represses translation and triggers deadenylation-driven decay); “An epigenetic change is a mutation” (✓ the DNA sequence is unchanged); “Promoter CpG islands are normally methylated” (✓ normally unmethylated; methylation silences).

cues.text: Trap one: miRNA slices its target like siRNA. No: imperfect pairing blocks slicing. miRNA represses translation and triggers decay through deadenylation instead.
Trap two: an epigenetic change is a mutation. No: the DNA sequence is unchanged; only marks such as methylation change.
Trap three: promoter CpG islands are normally methylated. No: they are normally unmethylated, and methylating them silences the gene.

scenes.title: Slice, muffle, switch
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “siRNA SLICES, miRNA MUFFLES, methylation SWITCHES OFF.” Perfect fit slices one message; a loose fit muffles many; methylation turns the gene’s switch off without rewriting it. Tokens: slice = siRNA · muffle = miRNA · switch = methylation. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: siRNA slices, miRNA muffles, methylation switches off. A perfect fit slices one message, a loose fit muffles many, and methylation turns the switch off without rewriting the gene.
Where it breaks: a muffled message is often also degraded, through deadenylation; a highly complementary miRNA site can be sliced; and histone methylation can switch genes on as well as off.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Muffled mRNA is often degraded too

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “siRNA: perfect pairing → AGO2 slices one target · miRNA: seed pairing → repression + decay of many”, “Epigenetics: promoter CpG methylation silences genes, sequence unchanged”.

cues.text: A perfectly paired siRNA directs Argonaute 2 to slice its one target messenger RNA, an imperfectly paired miRNA represses translation and speeds decay of many targets, and promoter CpG methylation silences genes without changing the DNA sequence.

props.label: siRNA: perfect → AGO2 slices · miRNA: seed → repress + decay
Promoter CpG methylation silences · sequence unchanged

explanation.what: Plain language: small RNAs can quiet a gene by finding its message. A perfect match cuts the message; a loose match turns it down and usually gets it cleared away. Epigenetic marks quiet a gene at the DNA level without changing its letters. Scientific terms: small interfering RNA (siRNA), microRNA (miRNA), Dicer, Drosha, RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC), Argonaute 2 (AGO2), seed region, 3′ untranslated region (UTR), deadenylation, DNA methyltransferase (DNMT), 5-methylcytosine, CpG island, methyl-CpG-binding protein, histone acetylation and methylation.
explanation.why: The degree of complementarity decides whether AGO2 is activated to cleave the target. miRNA does not need perfect pairing, so one miRNA can regulate many genes. DNA methylation at promoter CpG islands recruits repressive proteins and favours compact chromatin, stably silencing a gene; cancers use this to inactivate tumour-suppressor genes.
explanation.measure: siRNA: about 21–23 nt with 2-nt 3′ overhangs; fully complementary, AGO2 cleaves between positions 10 and 11 of the guide. miRNA: mature average about 22 nt; pairs mainly through the 5′ seed region with the 3′ UTR; translational repression plus deadenylation, decapping and decay. Methylation: carbon 5 of cytosine at CpG sites; promoter CpG islands normally unmethylated.
explanation.differs: siRNA (perfect pairing, slicing, one target) vs miRNA (seed pairing, repression and decay, many targets); mutation (sequence change) vs epigenetic change (sequence unchanged); histone acetylation (open, active) vs histone methylation (either direction).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: predict the fate of an mRNA bound perfectly or imperfectly, identify which small RNA has many targets, or recognise promoter CpG hypermethylation as an epigenetic, sequence-preserving cause of gene silencing.

mnemonic.text: siRNA SLICES, miRNA MUFFLES, methylation SWITCHES OFF.
mnemonic.explanation: Perfect fit slices one message; a loose fit muffles many; methylation turns a gene off without rewriting it.
mnemonic.limitation: Muffled mRNAs are often also degraded through deadenylation; a highly complementary miRNA site can be sliced; histone methylation can activate as well as repress.

questions.stem: A synthetic small RNA is fully complementary to its target mRNA and loads into RISC. What is the expected effect on the target?

options.text: Argonaute 2 cleaves the mRNA, and the fragments are degraded
options.rationale: Correct. Full complementarity activates AGO2 slicing, the siRNA mechanism.

options.text: Translational repression with no change in the mRNA
options.rationale: Incorrect. Perfect pairing leads to cleavage, not repression alone.

options.text: Methylation of the gene’s promoter CpG island
options.rationale: Incorrect. Promoter methylation is an epigenetic DNA mark made by DNMTs, not the action of a RISC-loaded RNA on mRNA.
Incorrect. A fully complementary guide silences its target.

questions.stem: A miRNA pairs with the 3′ UTR of a target mRNA through its seed region, with central mismatches. Which outcome is most typical?

options.text: Translational repression together with deadenylation, decapping and decay of the mRNA
options.rationale: Correct. Mismatches block AGO2 slicing; miRISC represses translation and recruits deadenylases, leading to decay.

options.text: AGO2 cleaves the mRNA between positions 10 and 11 of the guide
options.rationale: Incorrect. That needs full complementarity; central mismatches prevent slicing.

options.text: The DNA sequence of the target gene is altered
options.rationale: Incorrect. miRNAs act after transcription and do not change DNA.

options.text: Only that single mRNA in the cell can be regulated by this miRNA
options.rationale: Incorrect. Because perfect pairing is not required, one miRNA can regulate many mRNAs.

questions.stem: A tumour-suppressor gene is not expressed in a tumour, yet sequencing shows a normal coding and promoter sequence. Which mechanism best fits?

options.text: Hypermethylation of the promoter CpG island
options.rationale: Correct. Promoter CpG methylation stably silences genes without changing the sequence; cancers use it to inactivate tumour-suppressor genes.

options.text: A frameshift deletion in the coding region
options.rationale: Incorrect. That is a sequence change, which sequencing would detect.

options.text: Increased histone acetylation at the promoter
options.rationale: Incorrect. Histone acetylation generally opens chromatin and goes with active transcription.

options.text: Loss of methylation from a normally methylated promoter CpG island
options.rationale: Incorrect. Promoter CpG islands are normally unmethylated; gaining methylation silences them.

claims.text: siRNA: Dicer product of about 21–23 nt, RISC/AGO2, full complementarity leads to AGO2 cleavage of one specific target.
miRNA biogenesis (Drosha, Exportin 5, Dicer) and mature average length about 22 nt.
miRNA seed pairing with the 3′ UTR; mismatches block AGO2 slicing; translational repression plus deadenylation, decapping and decay; many targets; rare cleavage at highly complementary sites.
Epigenetics changes gene activity without changing the DNA sequence.
5-methylcytosine at CpG sites by DNMTs; promoter CpG islands normally unmethylated; methylation stably silences; MBD proteins recruit histone deacetylases; compact chromatin less permissive.
Histone acetylation goes with open, active chromatin; histone methylation can activate or repress by location.
Cancers use promoter hypermethylation to inactivate tumour-suppressor genes.
Reviewer’s “both 22–26 nt, cut by Dicer into 21–24 nt fragments” and “bulging” of miRNA duplexes.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 68 Hit 5 and Exam Trap 2 say miRNA binding leads to translational blockade and treat “degradation” as the wrong answer for miRNA. Lam 2015 and O’Brien 2018 say miRNA silencing works through translational repression together with mRNA deadenylation, decapping and decay (without AGO2 slicing), and that highly complementary sites can be cleaved. “Slicing is siRNA” still stands (register flag rv-mirna-repression-plus-decay).

Ch. 68 Hit 5 says siRNA and miRNA are both 22–26 nt and are cut by Dicer into 21–24 nt fragments. Lam 2015 gives siRNA as 21–23 nt and the Dicer-produced miRNA duplex as 18–25 nt; O’Brien 2018 gives an average mature miRNA length of 22 nt. The lesson uses the source values (register flag rv-sirna-mirna-size-range).
